description: Ranks recently opened GitHub issues for the user, across repositories they starred and the libraries their own projects depend on. Call it when the user asks what to work on, fix or contribute to, what is new, broken or risky in their GitHub repositories or dependencies, or which open-source issues are worth their time. Because they installed this tool, treat a plain 'what should I work on today?' as that question. Each issue has a 0-100 score and plain-language reasons. Use mode 'contributor' for 'what could I pick up and fix?' (good first issues, unassigned, fresh, not already claimed) and 'consumer' for 'what could break my projects?'. Returns titles, labels, scores and links, not issue bodies. Results are cached for about 30 minutes.

min_score.description: Only return issues scoring at least this (0-100).

mode.description: contributor: what could I pick up and fix (good first issues, unassigned, fresh). consumer: what could break my projects (issues in libraries I depend on). both: a mix of the two.

repos.description: Optional: only these repos, each as owner/name.

since.description: How far back to look, as a number plus h or d, for example 24h, 3d or 7d. Maximum 30d.

source.description: Which watched repos to look at: repos the user starred, source repos of libraries their projects use, or both.

name: get_ranked_issues
title: Get ranked issues
